properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-25, choosing between four homes and three timings.

═══ WHERE IT LIVES: a Decision that GOVERNS ═══

"We are building for reliability, because a lost reading cannot be recovered" is a choice with a rationale that shapes other nodes — which is an ADR, not a measurement. Decisions already GOVERN, so allocation, components and seams can each point at it; `what_next` already reads accepted Decisions; and nothing new is invented.

REJECTED, with the reasons: a **Constraint** (the KPP shape) treats the primary ility as a hard limit, but the design holds exactly ONE Constraint node and this would lean the answer on the least-exercised vocabulary in the project. **DimensionAssessment** was the cheapest in vocabulary terms and is the trap: its declared meaning is a SCORE of what IS, and giving it a second meaning — a TARGET — is the overload that made `Interface.designation` ambiguous, where an unclassified boundary and a deliberately internal one became indistinguishable.

⭐ THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDED IT: an assessment says what the system IS on an axis; a target says what it is FOR. Nothing held the second. Measured the same day: **0 DimensionAssessment and 0 DimensionObservation nodes exist** — the nine-axis enum has been fully defined, attachable to any node, and never once used.

═══ WHEN IT IS ASKED: at genesis, upfront ═══

Anthony, 2026-08-08: *"if you don't ask upfront, these cost a lot in having to rework services after they've been already developed."*

🛑 AND THIS DOES NOT CONTRADICT `dec:idea-allocation-waits-for-the-last-responsible-moment`, which is the objection to answer. That decision governs when you ALLOCATE. This governs when you learn what the system is FOR. **Asking is cheap and shapes everything downstream; allocating is expensive and can still wait.** Conflating the two would either force premature structure or lose the answer that structure needs.

═══ WHY IT NEEDS A PLACE OF ITS OWN, AND THE PRECEDENT ═══

The answer must be findable by a detector, or nothing notices when genesis skips the question — the failure this project has now measured three times in one month. `Decision.no_relation_note` was added to this same node type for exactly this reason, and its schema comment states the principle: *"prose cannot be told apart from silence, so the judgement gets a place of its own."* A primary ility recorded only in prose is in the same position.

📌 WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: whether the allocation step needs a skill of its own. It settles the FIRST STEP of one — the question that must precede any method — and leaves the method open at `dec:idea-does-the-deferred-structuring-step-need-a-skill-of-its-own`. Of the four ility branches only maintainability is runnable today (co-change, no instrumentation); performance needs coupling data almost no design declares; reliability and security have no substrate at all.
properties.name: DECIDED — what a system is FOR is recorded as a governing Decision, and asked at genesis rather than at allocation
properties.rationale:
Settled by the user against recorded alternatives, so the losing options and their reasons are kept — a later reader asking "why not DimensionAssessment, it already exists?" finds the overload argument rather than re-deriving it.

Recorded as a Decision rather than a Requirement because it is a choice about how this design records something, not a statement of what the system must do. The thing it decides — that an ility target is itself a governing Decision — is the same kind of node, which is deliberate: the mechanism and the record of choosing it are consistent.
